creator: rerating-catalysts
snapshot: India's largest IT services company by revenue; diversified across BFSI, Manufacturing, Retail/CPG, CMT, Life Sciences & Healthcare; promoter (Tata Sons) holding stable; PE (TTM) 15.86x, among the cheapest in large-cap IT.

catalysts.name: Q2FY27 results beat — revenue +11.2% YoY, PAT +15.0% YoY
catalysts.body: Consolidated revenue ₹73,188 Cr (Q2FY27) vs ₹72,275 Cr (Q1FY27, +1.3% QoQ) vs ₹65,799 Cr (Q2FY26, +11.2% YoY). PAT (shareholders) ₹13,884 Cr vs ₹13,349 Cr QoQ (+4.0%) vs ₹12,075 Cr YoY (+15.0%). Diluted EPS ₹38.37 vs ₹33.37 YoY.
catalysts.impact: PAT +15.0% YoY, EPS +15.0% YoY — broad-based, not segment-concentrated
catalysts.forwardMarker: If Q3FY27 YoY PAT growth drops back below double digits, treat this quarter's acceleration as a one-off rather than a trend.

catalysts.name: Second interim dividend ₹12/share declared
catalysts.body: Record date 14-Oct-2026, payment 30-Oct-2026. Continues TCS's shareholder-return cadence; not itself an EPS catalyst but signals confidence in cash generation.

noiseItems.subject: Date of payment of Dividend / Corporate Action — Board approves Dividend / Press Release
noiseItems.note: duplicate filings of the same results/dividend event, no incremental information

whatsInThePrice: At 15.86x TTM PE, TCS trades at a discount to its own 5-year average and to Infosys/HCLTECH on a growth-adjusted basis. A clean double-digit YoY PAT beat on an already-cheap multiple is constructive, but this is confirmation of steady compounding (framework's 'steady/normal' bucket), not a re-rating trigger — the market is unlikely to re-price TCS's multiple meaningfully off one in-line-to-good quarter alone.

risks.risk: US/European IT spending environment — discretionary project deferrals
risks.mitigant: TCS's BFSI/cost-takeout mix has historically been more resilient than discretionary-heavy peers

risks.risk: Currency (INR/USD, cross-currency) volatility on reported growth
AI-led pricing deflation in traditional application/BPO services
risks.mitigant: TCS's own AI tooling (ignio, ADD) repositions some of this as a margin lever rather than pure headwind — unverified this run

verdict: A genuinely good quarter — broad-based double-digit revenue and PAT growth, continued dividend cadence — but not a re-rating event. TCS sits in the framework's steady/normal growth bucket; this quarter confirms the compounding thesis rather than introducing a new EPS-accretive fact. Delivery-backed buying today (₹1,127.51 Cr, 47.51% of volume) reflects genuine institutional participation in the results, consistent with 'explained' linkage, not speculation.
jCurveReason: PAT +15.0% YoY and EPS +15.0% YoY (Q2FY27) are a genuine beat but fall well short of the framework's 30%-YoY PAT-growth threshold for a J-curve inflection; TCS is a steady/normal-bucket compounder, not a hyper-growth re-rating candidate this quarter.
